instruction: Merge only the odd-numbered .txt files (1.txt, 3.txt, 5.txt) from the VS Code project into a document 'odd_merge.docx' on the Desktop using LibreOffice Writer. Set the font size to 12.

required_snippets: Artistic expression serves as a window
forbidden_snippets: pursuit of knowledge is a noble endeavor

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully merged all 5 .txt files into concat.docx on Desktop using VS Code terminal and LibreOffice Writer, set font size to 10, and saved as .docx format.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use VS Code terminal to concatenate files, open LibreOffice Writer, select all text, change font size, save as .docx via Save As dialog, navigate file system.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests selective file merging (subset of files) with a different font size, requiring the agent to discriminate which files to include.
metadata.explanation: Task requires merging only odd-numbered .txt files (1, 3, 5) into a docx. Evaluator checks: (1) content from 1.txt, 3.txt, 5.txt is present, (2) content from 2.txt, 4.txt is absent, (3) font size is 12.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the docx file from the expected path (/home/user/Desktop/odd_merge.docx) and extracts both text content and font sizes using python-docx.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses required_snippets, forbidden_snippets, and expected_font_size from the rules dict without wrapping.

All three instruction requirements are covered: (1) required content from odd files via required_snippets (0.4 weight), (2) absence of even file content via forbidden_snippets (0.3 weight), (3) font size = 12 via expected_font_size (0.3 weight).
Scoring weights and partial credit logic are reasonable and well-structured.

Minor concern: getter only collects font sizes from runs where run.font.size is not None. Runs with inherited/default styles (font.size=None) are silently skipped, which could cause the font_sizes list to be empty even when the document has a valid font size set at the style level. In that case, the font check gives 0 points (not a false positive, but potentially too strict).
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking paragraph-level or style-level font sizes in the getter as a fallback when run.font.size is None, to handle inherited font sizes more robustly.
